# docs/ index — report register

Every report in `docs/` gets one line here, **newest first**. `analysis/` = our measurements,
`research/` = external synthesis.

**This file is generated** by [`reindex.py`](reindex.py) from each report's `<!-- meta -->`
block (date + one-line takeaway) — don't hand-edit the lists below. After adding or editing a
report, run `docs/reindex.py` (or `docs/reindex.py --check` in CI). Reports without a meta block
make reindex fail on purpose.

Format: `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM · kind · [file](path) — one-line takeaway`

- 2026-10-31 17:45 · analysis · [reasoning-replay-sharp-template-cactus-loops](analysis/2026-10-31-1745-reasoning-replay-sharp-template-cactus-loops.md) — Transcript-only analysis of seven W2-08 agentic runs (no GPU). (1) Old reasoning is rarely needed. Only 3.4-6.7% of the identifiers a step emits existed solely in thinking two or more steps back, and a keep-newest (k=1) run re-derives 3.6% on its own. A blind judge rated 6 of 32 keep-all reuse cases real dependencies, all from a running findings ledger (2 of them risky), and 0 of 8 in the k=1 run. A written conclusion of ≤15% would have kept everything later steps used in 7 of 10 blocks; the block's own last paragraph in only 2 of 10. → k=1 plus an externalized findings ledger. (2) "sharp" is a third-party template: froggeric v22.5 plus a 3-line TERSENESS system block. Its measured effect is −35-38% work with no demonstrated quality change (+2 findings, below the pre-registered ≥5) and weaker severity calibration. Five clauses can over-reach in an agent run; a scoped wording is proposed for an A/B. (3) The buun Qwen3.6 template disables thinking whenever tools are present by default, and blanks thinking after two short error-looking tool results (our tsc/eslint probes trigger it). Not usable as-is. (4) Cactus δ0.5 loops are inherent to its lossy acceptance rule, not a code bug. On 1.8.1 any drafted token with target p ≥ 0.5 is accepted with certainty, so a loop has no exit (0 of 3 top loops escaped, all hit 64k). The 1.9.1 cap restores half the stock escape, but 4 of the 6 measured 1.9.1 loop onsets were before the fade start (4,096 tokens). Under the cap, δ0.3 equals δ0.5 for every drafted token with p ≥ 0.29. (5) Correction: δ0.3's "15.8% loop signal" was repeated import lines, not a loop; δ 0 runs show 13.8-15.8% repeated-line blocks with no loop either.

On search and agent tasks the gain can be large (Tau² 87 vs 64). "Keep all" is not the optimum, though. The only Qwen3.x comparison (Sly 1.9.1) puts keep-newest-only at 25/32 multi-turn tasks, keep-all at 22/32 and drop-all at 17/32. Its no-result (loop) rate is 6/64 for keep-newest vs 35/64 for keep-all. A long-agent paper found full history (0.627) worse than deleting all reasoning (0.718) or entropy-pruning 80% of it (0.738). No published curve exists for keep-last-k with k=2..N. Recommendation for our Qwen3.8-27B Claude Code sessions: keep the newest turn only (k=1, sly2 rule), and test k=2-3 only if recall failures show up. Keep-all is unsafe with Cactus δ>0 and doubles context growth.

(3) Agentic step counts vary run to run (CV ~15% at best, snippet); ~6 runs per arm is established practice.

The real finding: Qwen recommends **32,768 output tokens** (81,920 for highly complex problems) while we run `--reasoning-budget 4096` and the model **saturates it every time** (3629–4095 MEASURED) — we have been truncating thinking ~8× below vendor guidance, a plausible driver of the erratic outputs. 16384 is the practical ceiling at 128k depth (32768 does NOT fit ctx 163840). `--reasoning-budget 0` is NOT "non-thinking mode": it forces an immediate end-of-thinking, whereas Qwen's non-thinking recipe (temp 0.7 / top_p 0.80 / presence_penalty 1.5) belongs to the `enable_thinking=false` template path — conflating them confounds budget with sampling.
